Description Hello Valve Development Team, I would like to report a possible issue with Dota 2's reporting and Behavior Score system. My Behavior Score recently dropped from 5,926 to 5,461, a loss of 465 points, and I received a temporary matchmaking restriction of approximately four hours. My latest Conduct Summary Matches evaluated: 15 Positive matches: 12 Reported matches: 3 Reports: 9 Reporting parties: 9 Communication reports: 0 Abandoned matches: 0 Commends: 21 Excessive Reports: Yes Description of the problem My account currently has communication restrictions due to its Behavior Score, meaning I cannot use text or voice chat. When teammates become toxic, I mute them, report inappropriate behavior when necessary, and continue playing normally. I use map pings to communicate gameplay information. Sometimes teammates repeatedly demand that I join fights that I believe are strategically unfavorable. When I choose not to participate in those fights to avoid unnecessary deaths, I suspect some teammates retaliate by reporting me. I understand that refusing a teammate's call does not automatically prove that their report is abusive. However, I am concerned that the reporting system may be penalizing legitimate strategic disagreements. Expected behavior Reports should be evaluated based on actual disruptive gameplay rather than simply disagreement between teammates. Actual behavior My account received nine reports across three reported matches, followed by a significant Behavior Score reduction and an approximately four-hour matchmaking restriction. I cannot confirm that these reports directly caused the restriction, but the timing raises concerns. Request Could the development team investigate whether the reporting system is correctly handling potentially retaliatory reports? If a system error is identified, I respectfully request that the resulting Behavior Score reduction and matchmaking restriction be reviewed and corrected where possible. Thank you for your time and consideration. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No Description Hello Valve developers, I would like to report a possible issue with the Behavior Score and Overwatch systems in Dota 2. On October 14, 2026, I received a 24-hour matchmaking ban with a notification stating that Overwatch had found me guilty of a gameplay violation. At the same time, my Behavior Score dropped from 2,215 to 1,465. However, my latest conduct summary shows the following statistics: - 15 matches played - 14 positive matches - Only 1 report - 39 commends - 0 abandoned matches - 0 communication reports - Excessive Reports: Yes I find this particularly confusing because the system marked my account as having excessive reports despite showing only one report in the latest summary. Recently, I have been playing Turbo matches to practice Invoker. I deliberately chose Turbo because I am still learning the hero and do not want to negatively affect other players in ranked or regular All Pick matches. I have not intentionally fed, griefed, or attempted to ruin anyone's games. I have simply been practicing a difficult hero while trying my best to win. I understand that making mistakes while learning a hero is normal, but I do not believe that poor performance alone should be treated as intentional griefing. I kindly ask the developers to investigate the following: 1. Why did my Behavior Score decrease despite having only one report and 39 commends? 2. Why was my account flagged with "Excessive Reports: Yes"? 3. Was the Overwatch punishment correctly applied? 4. Is there a possible issue affecting players with already low Behavior Scores? If this punishment was issued incorrectly, I would appreciate a review and restoration of the Behavior Score points that were unfairly deducted. I have attached a screenshot of my conduct summary as supporting evidence. System information - Device: MacBook Pro with Apple M2 - Hardware model: Mac14,7 - Operating system: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) - Architecture: x86-64 (translated through Rosetta 2) - Graphics renderer shown in crash report: Vulkan via MoltenVK - System Integrity Protection: Enabled - Game: Dota 2 through Steam Steps to reproduce 1. Launch Steam on macOS. 2. Open Dota 2. 3. Enter a match. 4. Play normally for approximately 2–5 minutes. 5. Dota 2 unexpectedly crashes. Troubleshooting attempted - Enabled the Dota 2 developer console. - Attempted the `tv_stop true` workaround. - Tested gameplay again. - The game continues to crash. Crash report details ```text Process: dota2 Identifier: com.valvesoftware.dota2 Code Type: X86-64 (Translated) OS Version: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) Exception Type: EXC_GUARD Exception Subtype: GUARD_TYPE_MACH_PORT Exception Message: INVALID_OPTIONS on mach port 0 Exception Codes: 0x0000000009c00000 0x8001430200000003 Termination Reason: Namespace GUARD Code 2305843022098595840 Triggered by Thread: 4 Thread 4: google_breakpad::ForwardException google_breakpad::ExceptionHandler::WaitForMessage Error Formulating Crash Report: RIP register does not match crashing frame ``` The crash report indicates that Valve's Breakpad exception handler encounters a Mach port guard violation. This may be masking an earlier crash within the game. The report also shows an active `HLTVServerAsync` thread, although I cannot confirm whether it contributes to the failure. Expected behavior Dota 2 should remain stable throughout matches on supported macOS systems. ### Actual behavior The game terminates unexpectedly after approximately 2–5 minutes of gameplay. Related issues - ValveSoftware/Dota2-Gameplay#34038 - ValveSoftware/Dota-2#3445 Request Please investigate this recurring gameplay crash affecting Dota 2 on Apple Silicon Macs running through Rosetta 2. Description Description: When a tradable/marketable Prismatic Gem (purchased via Steam Community Market with real money) is socketed into a non-tradable item (such as an Arcana received from a Battle Pass / Swag Bag), and later removed from that item, the gem permanently inherits the "Not Tradable / Not Marketable" restriction from the host item. The core issue: At no point during the socketing process, nor during the extraction/removal process, is the user given any warning that this action will permanently revoke the tradable/marketable status of their own separately purchased item. This results in real financial loss for players who paid real money for these gems, with no way to reverse the outcome. Steps to reproduce: Purchase a Prismatic Gem via Steam Community Market (tradable/marketable). Socket the gem into an Arcana that is itself non-tradable (e.g., received from a Battle Pass/Swag Bag). Later, use an Artificer's Hammer to destroy/recycle the Arcana in order to retrieve the gem. Observe that the extracted gem is now permanently marked "Not Tradable / Not Marketable," despite being fully tradable before this process. Expected behavior: Either: The gem should retain its original tradable/marketable status after being removed from a non-tradable item, since it was never part of the free/non-tradable item itself, OR At minimum, a clear and explicit warning should be shown before socketing or before destruction, specifically informing the user that their own paid item will become permanently non-tradable/non-marketable as a result. Actual behavior: The gem becomes permanently non-tradable/non-marketable with zero warning or disclosure at any step of the process, resulting in a loss of real monetary value for the user with no way to reverse the action. Additional context: I contacted Steam Support regarding this issue and was informed that this is "by design" and cannot be changed through support channels, and was advised to report this here Account ID: 114342752 Observed score changes * My Behavior Score remained close to the maximum of 12,000. * My Communication Score dropped from 12,000 to approximately 7,300 within seven days — a decrease of roughly 4,700 points. * For approximately a year before this period, my Communication Score fluctuations had generally been no more than around 500 points. * My communication features were temporarily restored when my score was approximately 8,200, but the score subsequently dropped again to 7,382. Conduct Summary evidence My documented Conduct Summary includes: * 0 abandons across the reviewed periods * 285 matches in the previously reviewed data * 692 commendations * 32 total reports and 26 Communication Reports in that earlier dataset * In the latest visible 15-match period: 14 positive matches, 1 reported match, 3 total reports, 9 Communication Reports from 7 reporting parties, and a Behavior Score of 11,997 The latest figures are from a newer period and should be considered separately from the earlier totals. Why I am reporting this I understand that Behavior Score and Communication Score are separate automated systems, and I am not claiming that these numbers alone prove a bug. However, the speed and magnitude of this decrease are substantially different from my previous score history. I would like to know whether this could be caused by an issue with Communication Report processing or score calculation. I really don’t get why there is a mechanic like this, it’s basically meant to be for griefers… why is everyone allowed to decrease your score and why we don’t have the Overwatch system for this too. It does not make any sense and ruins the game for me. I play the game since 2013 and even before, but that’s the official start, I never ever was not able to communicate with my team in 13 years, but now suddenly in 1 week i lose half of my communication rights? Honestly this does noch fit and does not make any sense at all. Since I am grown up now and I am not toxic at all… Could the Dota 2 team clarify whether this behavior is expected and whether there is a way to verify that reports contributing to a Communication Score were processed correctly? I am not requesting a manual score increase or an MMR adjustment. I am asking for clarification about a potentially abnormal result in the reporting system. I have screenshots of my score history and Conduct Summary available as evidence. Thank you for your time. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 9026083911 02. Each one cost me roughly 1,000 Behavior Score points and sent me to Low Priority. This is the data from my own Personal Game Data page (Conduct Summary): | Summary date (GMT) | Reported matches | Reports | Commends | Behavior Score | Change | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Sep 19, 15:04 | 0 | 0 | 29 | 7,249 | — | | Sep 20, 10:33 | 2 | 5 | 25 | 6,561 | −688 | | Sep 20, 21:49 | 3 | 6 | 24 | 5,548 | −1,013 | | Sep 21, 21:34 | 1 | 2 | 27 | 5,295 | −253 | | Sep 23, 10:32 | 3 | 7 | 23 | 5,270 | −25 | | Sep 23, 14:16 | 3 | 7 | 27 | 4,345 | −925 | | Sep 30, 08:10 | 2 | 4 | 25 | 4,238 | −107 | | Oct 1, 10:17 | 3 | 8 | 28 | 3,300 | −938 | Some things this table shows clearly: - In every single summary, 12 to 15 of my 15 matches were positive. The problem is 1–3 lost games out of every 15. - I received 23–29 commends in every summary. Most of my teammates were fine playing with me. - I received only ONE communication report in this whole period. I was not flaming or toxic in chat. These are gameplay reports from lost games. - Almost the entire 3,949-point drop comes from four large penalties of roughly −700 to −1,000 each. ## The matches **Match 9008909843 (Sep 20) — Wraith King, 3/6/9, lost.** Three of my teammates were in one party (Spirit Breaker, Lina, Templar Assassin). I had the second-highest hero damage on my team (13.2k) and died less than three of my teammates. The Templar Assassin from that party went 1/4/5 with the lowest hero damage on the team (5.0k). After this game I got an Overwatch penalty, Low Priority, and the next summary took −1,013 from me. **Match 9007822317 (Sep 20) — Dragon Knight, 2/11/13, lost.** I will be honest: this was a bad game for me. But I played until the end. I did not go AFK, I did not feed on purpose, I did not destroy items, I did not abandon. A bad game is not griefing. I was still convicted and sent to Low Priority, the second time that same day. **Match 9012524823 (Sep 23) — Wraith King, 7/15/7, lost.** Yes, I died a lot. But I also had the second-highest hero damage (25.1k) and the highest tower damage (1.9k) on my team. Again: −925. **Match 9024164970 (Oct 1) — Wraith King, 4/12/14, lost.** My last game before quitting. Our team was ahead by up to 6k net worth until about minute 27, then we lost the game in late fights. I had 30.7k hero damage, second on my team. Our support died 17 times. At the same time, in my games I regularly see teammates who stand AFK, destroy their items, build a Rapier and lose it to the enemy, or move items around to troll. As far as I can see, nothing happens to them. ## Why this system feels completely unfair 1. **There is no appeal.** Steam Support says it does not review or remove Overwatch restrictions. There is no other channel. One click from a few random players plus a quick review can take 1,000 points from a 4,000-hour player, and there is nothing I can do about it. 2. **I am never told which match I was convicted for, or why.** The notification only says "a match you recently played". I have to guess from when my Low Priority games started. How am I supposed to "improve my behavior" if I am not told what the behavior was? 3. **Bad play is punished like griefing.** I play offlane, often alone against two heroes. Dying several times early in a solo lane looks like "feeding" in a short replay fragment, but it is just Dota. Losing a lane is not a crime. 4. **Party stacks have too much power against solo players.** A group that is losing can easily push a solo player into Overwatch. 5. **It is a death spiral.** The lower my score, the worse my teammates, the more often games collapse, the more reports I get, the lower my score. Once you fall, the system pushes you further down. 6. **The punishment and the recovery are completely out of proportion.** One conviction costs about 1,000 points. A clean game gives about 10–13 points. That means one conviction erases 80–100 clean games. To get back to where I was just 12 days ago, I would need 300–400 games with ZERO reports, which is 250–330 hours of playing with one thought in my head: "please, nobody press report". ## How this makes me feel Honestly, I am angry and exhausted. I feel helpless. I have spent thousands of hours on this game because I loved it, and now every match feels like an exam where four strangers decide whether I lose a week of progress. I cannot enjoy a game where I have to play not to win, but to avoid making anyone upset after a loss. That is not Dota anymore. The joy is completely gone. ## About money Over the years I have regularly spent money on Dota 2. I supported the game because I believed in it. As of today, that is over. I will not spend anything more on Dota 2 while the behavior system works like this. ## What I am asking for 1. **A real appeal process** for Overwatch convictions, with a human review on request. 2. **Transparency:** tell the player which match they were convicted for and which behavior was the reason. 3. **A clear line between "bad game" and "griefing".** Deaths alone, or losing a lane, should not be enough for a conviction. 4. **Full context for Overwatch reviewers**, not a short fragment of the match. 5. **Accountability for reviewers** who vote "guilty" on almost every case without real review. 6. **Less weight for reports from party stacks against solo players**, and the Avoid Party protection in all modes. 7. **Proportional recovery**, so one bad week does not take hundreds of hours to fix. 8. If possible, please review my account and my recent convictions. I am writing this not just for myself, but because I see many players with exactly the same story. Please fix this system. Right now it is pushing long-time players out of the game. Thank you for reading, Description Hello Dota 2 Development Team, I would like to report an issue with the Legacy Key system and Quick Cast. There are currently two problems that I have noticed: 1. Missing Legacy Key for the new hero The newly added hero does not appear to have a proper Legacy Key assignment for the abilities. Players who use Legacy Keys have to manually work around the missing key assignments, which makes it difficult to use the hero with the same control setup as other heroes. Please consider adding a proper Legacy Key configuration for the new hero. 2. Quick Cast + Legacy Keys are not working correctly Recently, Quick Cast has stopped working properly when Legacy Keys are enabled. I normally use Legacy Keys together with Quick Cast, but now the combination does not behave as it used to. This makes the control setup especially difficult for players who have been using Legacy Keys for a long time. The issue appears to be related specifically to the interaction between Legacy Keys and Quick Cast, rather than Quick Cast itself. Expected behavior When Legacy Keys are enabled, each ability should have its corresponding Legacy Key, and Quick Cast should activate the ability immediately when the assigned key is pressed, just as it does with the normal keybind system. Actual behavior The new hero does not have a proper Legacy Key assignment. Quick Cast does not work correctly with Legacy Keys. This makes it difficult or impossible to use the new hero with the same Legacy Key + Quick Cast setup that players have used previously. Please investigate whether there was a recent change that affected the interaction between Legacy Keys and Quick Cast. I would really appreciate it if the Legacy Key assignments for the new hero could be added and the Quick Cast + Legacy Keys behavior could be restored to how it worked previously. Thank you for your work on Dota 2. I purchased a Battle Cup Ticket because I wanted to play in the Battle Cup. However, after paying for the ticket, I am being told that I cannot participate because of my low Behavior Score. I would like to file a formal complaint about the current Behavior Score system in Dota 2, as well as the fact that my low Behavior Score is preventing me from using a Battle Cup Ticket that I have already paid for. I understand that Dota 2 needs a system to deal with toxic behavior and reports. However, I believe the current system is unfair in my situation and creates a cycle that makes it extremely difficult to improve my Behavior Score. I have played my matches respectfully and have always tried to win. I do not intentionally insult, harass or disrespect other players. In fact, I currently cannot even use chat properly, so I have very limited ability to communicate with other players in the first place. This creates a serious problem: if another player asks me something or expects communication from me, I may not be able to respond. I can then still receive reports because I did not communicate, even though the reason I did not communicate is that the system itself restricts my ability to do so. There is also a problem when playing with a group. Communication is restricted in the lobby, even in situations where players are simply trying to coordinate before or around a match. This makes it even harder to communicate normally and demonstrate positive behavior. Another issue is that players can receive reports simply because a game was lost or because teammates blame a particular player, such as the carry. Losing a match does not automatically mean that a player behaved badly or intentionally played poorly. A report system should distinguish between actual toxic behavior and normal gameplay disagreements, mistakes, or losing a match. Most importantly, I currently feel trapped in a cycle: * My Behavior Score is low. * Because of the low score, my communication is restricted. * I can't communicate in the lobby with my party in certain situations, including when we are trying to coordinate around the lobby. This makes the situation even more frustrating. * Because I cannot communicate normally, I cannot properly respond to teammates or demonstrate positive communication. * I can still receive reports for not communicating. * Because of the reports/restrictions, my Behavior Score does not improve. * At the same time, I am prevented from using content that I have actually paid for, such as my Battle Cup Ticket. I have been trying to get out of this situation for a long time, but I cannot seem to make meaningful progress. I would like Dota 2 Support to explain how a player is realistically supposed to recover from this situation. I am not asking for the Behavior Score system to be removed. I am asking for a fair and realistic way for players to recover when they are restricted, especially when they are making a genuine effort to play respectfully. I also believe that if a player is prevented from participating in a paid feature because of their Behavior Score, there should be a clear warning before the purchase is made. I purchased the Battle Cup Ticket, but I am now unable to use it. Please review my account and my Behavior Score history, including the reports and communication restrictions applied to my account. I would also like you to consider whether the current restrictions are preventing me from improving the very score that is causing those restrictions. I would appreciate a concrete solution rather than simply being told to "increase my Behavior Score", because under the current restrictions I do not see a realistic way to do that. Thank you. Description Hello. I have been playing Dota 2 for a long time, and I am writing not to dispute a ban or complain about a specific match. I want to draw attention to a problem in the Communication Score and report system that, in my view, harms the game and punishes innocent players. I agree that Behavior Score is a working and necessary thing. It genuinely restrains those who ruin games: AFK players, feeders, people who intentionally spoil the match. But Communication Score works differently, and here is the fundamental problem. Dota 2 is a team game where communication is critical. When a player is forcibly deprived of the ability to write and speak, it is not only he who suffers, but also his four teammates. You cannot call missing, you cannot warn about a gank, you cannot call for Roshan, you cannot coordinate a push. So the punishment of one person turns into a punishment for the entire team. At the same time, the game already has a mute button. Any player can mute any teammate or opponent and no longer see or hear them. It turns out that the forced silence system duplicates a function that every player already has, but does it for everyone at once, without their consent. A separate problem is the mechanism of reports for communication itself. It does not analyze what exactly a person wrote or said. A report triggers based on the number of complaints. Because of this, a "communication report" easily turns into a tool of revenge: a person can be reported for bad play, for an incomprehensible move, for disagreeing with someone's decision- and he will receive a silence, even though he insulted no one. This has been discussed in the community for a long time, including by well-known players and streamers. Dendi publicly said that the report system "just doesn't work"; Stray228 compared forced mute in a team game to a situation where a footballer is left on the field but forbidden to pass. So on paper, the idea of separating "behavior" and "communication" looks logical. The problem is in the execution: the system triggers too easily on false complaints and gives a normal player almost no opportunity to prove that he did nothing wrong. What, in my opinion, should be changed: 1)Remove the forced global mute, or at least make it "off by default," so that teammates can decide for themselves whether to hear this player or not. 2)Make it so that a communication report triggers only with real analysis of text or voice, and not based on the number of complaints. 3)Leave players under silence with basic pings and the chat wheel- they are not toxicity and are needed for the game. 4)Return reports to their original meaning: to punish for ruining the game, not for an "unpleasant manner of communication." I understand that this is not a technical support issue, but I ask you to forward this to the Dota 2 team. Thank you for the game and for actually reading feedback. Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I am reporting a problem with the current Overwatch and behavior restriction system and, more specifically, the lack of transparency or an appeal/review mechanism for players who receive an Overwatch conviction. I have been playing Dota 2 since November 4, 2012, and this account has been part of my gaming history for almost 14 years. Recently, my Behavior Score dropped from 7,987 to 3,077 in a relatively short period of time. During this period I received multiple Low Priority penalties, and my communication features were eventually disabled. The most recent penalty was particularly concerning because it was issued after an Overwatch review. The match in question is: Match ID: 9001535070 Hero: Outworld Destroyer Result: Victory Score: 23 / 4 / 15 MVP Reports: 2 Commends: 28 After contacting Steam Support, I specifically asked them to investigate what happened to my account or, if Steam Support could not investigate Overwatch decisions, to provide me with a way to contact the team responsible for reviewing them. Steam Support confirmed that the matchmaking restriction was caused by an Overwatch conviction and later confirmed that the conviction was based on this exact match (9001535070). However, Steam Support also told me that: - they do not review or remove Overwatch restrictions; - they cannot provide contact information for the Overwatch team; - and there is no alternative appeal channel they can provide. I understand that Steam Support may not have the ability to manually remove an Overwatch restriction. I am not asking for special treatment or for Valve to simply remove my penalty because I disagree with it. My concern is the lack of transparency. If an Overwatch conviction is based on a specific match, I believe the affected player should at least be able to understand what behavior was considered a violation. At the moment, I have no information about: 1. What specific behavior in match 9001535070 resulted in the conviction. 2. What category of violation was identified. 3. What part or timestamp of the replay was considered evidence. 4. Whether the conviction was reviewed by multiple reviewers or how the verdict was validated. 5. Whether there is any mechanism to challenge an incorrect Overwatch verdict. I fully understand that a good KDA, winning a match, or receiving MVP does not automatically prove that no violation occurred. I am therefore not claiming that my statistics alone prove the conviction was wrong. The problem is that I have no way to determine what I supposedly did wrong in the first place. This is especially concerning because the affected player cannot meaningfully learn from or challenge a decision when the only information provided is that an Overwatch conviction occurred. There is also an important context regarding my recent Behavior Score history. Between two of my recent conduct summaries, my Behavior Score changed from 3,902 to 3,077. During those seven matches I won 6 out of 7 games. The final match in that sequence was the Outworld Destroyer game mentioned above, which was a 23/4/15 victory with 28 commends and 2 reports. Again, I am not presenting this as proof that the Overwatch verdict must be wrong. I am providing it because the circumstances make it particularly important for me to understand what behavior was actually reviewed and why it resulted in a conviction. I am also a long-time Dota 2 streamer and content creator. Because I regularly stream my games, I have experienced situations where viewers or other players intentionally watch the stream and interact with the game around it. I cannot prove that this caused the reports or the Overwatch conviction, so I am not presenting it as a fact. However, I believe it is a relevant possibility when investigating unusual reporting patterns on a streaming account. I am not asking Valve to reveal the identities of Overwatch reviewers or any private information about them. I am asking for a reasonable way for an affected player to understand and, when appropriate, challenge an Overwatch decision. My questions to the Dota 2 team are therefore: - Is there currently any way for a player to obtain information about the specific violation that resulted in an Overwatch conviction? - Is there any mechanism for reviewing or appealing a potentially incorrect Overwatch verdict? - How does Valve ensure that Overwatch convictions are sufficiently validated before they result in matchmaking restrictions and major Behavior Score penalties? - If a conviction is found to be incorrect, is there any mechanism to correct the resulting Behavior Score or other penalties? I have been playing Dota 2 for almost 14 years and I genuinely do not want to leave the game because of a punishment that I cannot understand or challenge. I would appreciate it if the Dota 2 team could clarify how this system is intended to work from the perspective of the player receiving the conviction. Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 9001535070 ### Screenshots Support (Ari) directed me to post this here because the current Behavior Score system has a fundamental design flaw at the ~3k level. The way the communication ban interacts with automated reports creates an impossible, inescapable loop for players who are genuinely trying to win and improve their score. **The Core Design Flaw: Playing with Bots** Communication is the absolute core of any multiplayer team game. When you completely remove a player's ability to communicate, you turn a team-based strategic game into a single-player experience. I might as well be playing against bots, because the interaction with my team is exactly the same. When you drop below 6,000 behavior score, you cannot ask for help, coordinate with your team, ping the map effectively, or explain macro decisions. Because you cannot explain your actions, teammates lacking map awareness automatically assume you are griefing, report you, and the automated system issues severe punishments with zero human oversight. **Case Study from a Recent Match:** To demonstrate how this algorithm fails, here is exactly what happened in my recent match. I played Axe offlane with a Phoenix support against a very tough Spectre and Enchantress lane. Phoenix was role-abusing, taking farm and last hits instead of helping me survive. From a gameplay design perspective, what is the intended correct play here? - **Option A:** Stand at a safe distance on the lane, get zero gold, and leech experience from my support (who can safely solo the lane due to range and escape skills). This is widely considered griefing. - **Option B:** Leave the unplayable lane, move to the jungle to recover, and let the support have the lane. I chose Option B. I stopped contesting Phoenix for farm and went to jungle. Because I was completely muted by the system, I couldn't tell my team why I was doing this. Here is how the situation escalated: - Phoenix followed me to the jungle to steal last hits from a triple-stacked camp I made. - He/she then moved to the safe lane to stand in trees, doing nothing, but to leech XP from our carries. - He/she went in to bushes to AFK for about 15 seconds from a middle of teamfight with full hp. I ended up doing the supports (Phoenix) work, buying 3 Observers and 6 Sentries, while the actual support bought exactly 2 Sentries in a 42-minute game. I also made several immediate buybacks after dying. Again, because I was muted, I couldn't explain that this was a deliberate macro strategy. Returning to the lane meant instant death from Spectre and Enchantress. Buying back allowed me to farm safer areas and stay close to the game's overall XP progression. The scoreboard at the end of the game proves this strategy worked: I successfully kept up with the level progression and was on the exact same level as everyone else. Once I got the relevant basic items (Vanguard, Blink Dagger to counter the 4 ranged enemies, and a Blade Mail), I rotated back, tanked damage, initiated fights, and we actually won the game. I was even commended by our carries. **The Automated Punishment & The Single Draft Trap:** Despite adapting to a griefing teammate, buying the wards, playing to the very end, and winning the game, the automated system immediately hit me with a 4-hour matchmaking ban, a -500 behavior score drop, and a Low Priority penalty requiring 3 Single Draft wins to escape. This Single Draft penalty is completely contradictory and feeds directly into the same broken loop: - You are forced to play with actual, legitimate griefers who are in Low Priority for the right reasons. - Because the hero pool is restricted, teammates frequently pick unsuitable heroes for the lineup, leading to setups with 4 or 5 hard carries. - People refuse to adapt their roles, or they simply have never played the random heroes they were given. - This inevitably leads to more griefing, ruined games, and consequently, more false reports from tilted teammates. - As a result, your behavior score continues to tank even further based on false reports while you are just trying to win your 3 mandatory matches. I am a 37-year-old man, and I do not believe I have ever been a toxic player. I do not throw rage fits, and I have never abandoned a match midway through unless there was a power outage (which hasn't happened in years). I am a team player—in non-role queue games, if everyone else picks a carry or a tank, I will always try to pick a support or whatever role the team is missing. To be completely honest, I do not even remember why my behavior score originally dropped to ~3000, because it happened several years ago. Since then, due to how this communication ban and punishment loop operates, it has been practically impossible to raise it back up. **The Mathematical Impossibility:** The most broken part of this system is the math behind recovering your score: - **The Grind:** If you manage to play 15 games without a single negative ping or false report, the system updates your score by about 250 points. That is roughly 12.5 hours of playing. - **The Punishment:** After this single match—where I didn't communicate at all, adapted to a bad lane, and won the game—I lost 500 points. - **The Result:** 25 hours of clean grinding wiped out by an automated algorithm in an instant. My score dropped back to 2,500. Now, on top of a 4-hour ban and the Single Draft prison, I am forced to play AT LEAST another 25 hours of unranked games just to unlock ranked matchmaking again, just for the exact same problem to repeat. **The "For Fun" Report Exploit:** The vulnerability of this automated system is public knowledge. There are multiple YouTube videos right now showing players admitting they report others purely for fun. They proudly showcase their "Action Taken" lists on screen, openly acknowledging that none of the players they reported actually did anything wrong—yet your automated system still punishes those innocent players based on malicious reports. **Conclusion** I completely understand that a multiplayer game needs a punishment system to keep the community healthy, but this current implementation is absolutely not the right way to do it. How can a player improve their behavior score when the system mutes them from explaining legitimate gameplay decisions, forces them into an endless 25-hour grind for minimal points, traps them in Single Draft with actual griefers, and empowers those griefers to hand out automated bans? I have played Dota for 14 years, but I have completely lost faith in how this game and its automated systems are being managed. I used to absolutely hate League of Legends, but this complete lack of respect for your player base has forced me to reconsider. It has become glaringly obvious that Valve only values high-ranked and professional players, while us paying, casual players who actually fund the game are completely ignored. You are simply riding on the legend of the game at this point. This fundamentally broken system is undoubtedly driving many dedicated players to League of Legends, and I am now one of them. I will be canceling my long-term subscription upon making this transition. Description **Request to rework or remove the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2** Hello Valve, I would like to ask you to seriously reconsider the current Communication/Behavior system in Dota 2. The problem is that a system designed to reduce toxicity has started to negatively affect one of the most important parts of Dota 2 - communication between teammates. Dota 2 is a team game. Players need to communicate constantly: call missing heroes, suggest objectives, coordinate Roshan, smokes, buybacks, item timings, team fights, lane swaps, defensive actions and dozens of other situations. However, the current system creates an environment where players are increasingly afraid to communicate at all. Players avoid using voice chat, text chat and sometimes even pings because any active interaction with teammates can potentially result in reports and a reduction of Communication Score. As a result, the safest way to protect your account and Behavior Score is simply to remain silent. This creates an absurd situation: **The optimal behavior in a competitive 5v5 team game is to avoid communicating with your team.** The consequences are clearly visible in matchmaking: * players rarely use voice chat; * important information is not communicated; * teammates do not discuss strategy; * players are afraid to criticize even obvious gameplay mistakes; * communication often starts only when the match is already lost; * coordinated play in solo matchmaking becomes significantly harder; * reports can effectively be used as a punishment for disagreement rather than actual toxic behavior. There is also an important distinction between **toxicity** and **communication that another player simply does not like**. Insults, harassment, racism, threats and intentional spam should obviously be punishable. But saying things such as: "Don't fight without buyback." "Please stop farming and come Roshan." "We need BKB before the next fight." "Don't go high ground now." "Can you TP bottom?" should not create a risk for a player's ability to communicate in future matches simply because another player disagreed with the call and decided to report them. The current system incentivizes silence instead of healthy team communication. I believe Valve should either substantially redesign this system or remove the communication restrictions in their current form. Possible improvements could include: 1. Separate actual toxic behavior from ordinary gameplay communication and disagreements. 2. Reduce the influence of mass communication reports when there is no evidence of abusive behavior. 3. Make Communication Score penalties more transparent so players understand exactly what behavior resulted in a restriction. 4. Do not remove essential team communication tools from players unless there is clear evidence of serious or repeated abuse. 5. Introduce stronger protection against report abuse after lost matches. 6. Evaluate the content and context of communication instead of relying primarily on the number of reports. 7. Preserve essential strategic communication such as voice, pings and gameplay calls wherever possible. Dota 2 is one of the most complex competitive team games ever created. Communication should be encouraged, not treated as a potential risk to the player's account. A system intended to combat toxicity should punish toxic behavior. It should not make silence the safest strategy. Please consider reviewing the current Communication/Behavior system and its impact on actual teamwork in matchmaking. Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots _No I do not understand what violation I supposedly committed and I strongly disagree with the verdict. Here is my recent match history from August 29: 20:54 — Tidehunter — WIN — 22:44 20:30 — Tiny — WIN — 16:31 20:03 — Razor — WIN — 14:00 19:22 — Shadow Fiend — LOSS — 28:54 All of these matches were Turbo games. I did not intentionally grief, feed, go AFK, destroy my items, abandon a match, or deliberately sabotage my team. If I made a mistake during a match, that should not automatically be considered intentional griefing. The main problem is that the Patrol notification provides absolutely no useful information about the alleged violation. I am not told: - Which Match ID was reviewed. - Which exact match resulted in the conviction. - What exact action was considered a violation. - At what timestamp the alleged violation happened. - What type of violation I was found guilty of. - What evidence the Patrol reviewers used. - How I can appeal an incorrect Patrol decision. I understand the purpose of Overwatch and I support using it against players who genuinely ruin games. However, an Overwatch system is only useful if its verdicts are accurate. Players can report others simply because they lost, disliked a hero pick, disagreed with an item build, disliked someone's playstyle, or were frustrated with their teammates. A player making mistakes or having a bad game is not the same thing as intentionally griefing. In my case, I believe the Patrol made an incorrect decision and I would like Valve to investigate it. Whether this Overwatch conviction can be reviewed if the verdict was incorrect. I am not asking Valve to blindly remove a legitimate punishment. If I actually violated a rule, I want to know exactly what I did and in which match. But if there was no intentional violation, then this is an example of a false Overwatch conviction and the resulting punishment should be reconsidered. Description There is a critical logical flaw in the automated Behavior Score system that causes a permanent soft-lock for solo queue players trapped below 3000 score. For the past 6 months, my account has been completely restricted from ranked matchmaking, voice chat, and text chat. Despite being physically unable to commit any communication abuse (due to the permanent system mute), my behavior score continues to drop or remains frozen at the absolute bottom. The automated system aggregates all reports blindly without assessing context. In low behavior brackets, solo queue players are constantly matched with pre-made party stacks (2, 3, or 4 players). When a party loses a match, they subjectively use the silent solo player as a scapegoat, issuing 3 to 4 reports simultaneously out of spite. The system treats this mass party report as a consensus of toxic behavior. This creates an inescapable mathematical deadlock: 1. To increase the behavior score, a player must play standard matches. 2. Playing standard matches as a solo queue player naturally triggers false, subjective reports from toxic party stacks. 3. The automated system accepts these reports (even for communication abuse on a completely muted account), lowering the score even further. Currently, the only way to escape this automated prison is to break Steam's ToS by paying third-party boosting services to play in a 5-man stack where reports are impossible. This is a technical system loop that cannot be resolved automatically. I kindly request a developer or technical administrator to review my account logs for the past 6 months, verify that I have not committed any genuine griefing (destroying items, running down mid), and manually adjust or reset my behavior score to a baseline level. Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I enjoy Dota and play it whenever I have free time. However, for several years now, I have been stuck in what feels like a nightmare of this game, with a Behavior Score fluctuating between 0 and 5,000. Since I don't play Ranked, I don't have the option to avoid parties. As many players know, party players tend to report solo players, shifting the blame for their own poor performance onto the one player who isn't in their group. This happens very often. Currently, I can't even reach 3,000 Behavior Score. It feels like the system intentionally places me in matches right when I'm about to hit that mark, matching me with a full party of four players — which means four reports. This leads me straight into Overwatch. And Overwatch, as it stands, almost always returns a guilty verdict. There are discussions where people admit they click "Guilty" on every case without reviewing the replay at all. As a result, you lose 1,000 points from the verdict, and the reports also throw you into Low Priority games, where you continue to get reported endlessly. In total, you lose around 1,500 points, and you're back to 1,000 Behavior Score. The cycle repeats endlessly, and there is simply no way out of it in the current state of the system. I see many other players reporting similar issues on your GitHub. About two months ago, I finally became so frustrated that I took a break after receiving 4 Low Priority games. I returned recently for the event and noticed that matchmaking had been reworked — I hoped the Behavior Score system had received some attention as well. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case. I struggled through those Low Priority games, managed to play 4 All Pick matches, and then received another punishment from Overwatch. In all 4 of those games, I was the only solo player on my team. There were constant pings directed at me, insults, and likely reports as well. I played well in all of those matches, and there was absolutely no valid reason for a penalty. I realize that nobody is going to review these games, but to support my claim, here is the Match ID from which I received the punishment: 8956143152. By the way, in that same match, the Terrorblade player destroys his items at 48:18. But naturally, no one will report him because he is playing with his friends in a party and can do whatever he wants — they are just having fun. I believe there are several ways to improve this system and potentially bring back hundreds, or even thousands, of players who have left because of these issues. For example: 1. Introduce a "Behavior Score Reset Token" as a reward in one of the events, at least once a year — for instance, in the Quartero's Curios event at level 150. This token would be non-tradable, non-giftable, and usable only once per account, setting the Behavior Score to its maximum value. Ruiners would drop back down in just a few games anyway, so this wouldn't harm normal players in any way. 2. Extend the "Avoid Party" feature to unranked matches, just as it already exists in Ranked. This would at least partially prevent situations where a solo player receives 4 reports and ends up in Overwatch, leading to automatic Low Priority games. 3. Increase the accountability and quality standards for Overwatch reviewers. Currently, there is no penalty for reviewers who hand out "Guilty" verdicts without properly reviewing the evidence. Implementing a quality check or a verification mechanism for Overwatch cases would ensure that only genuine griefers are punished, and innocent players are not caught in a faulty automated loop. I see many posts here about the flaws in the Behavior Score system, and I truly hope you take this feedback into consideration. Thank you for your time and for this incredible Description The current Communication/Behavior Score system and its automated in-game mutes are actively hurting the matchmaking experience. Dota 2 is a highly competitive, team-oriented game that requires constant communication. The problems with the current mute system are: 1. System Abuse: The automated mute system is easily abused. Players frequently use communication reports to punish teammates for bad gameplay (missed spells, lost lanes), rather than actual toxicity. 2. Collateral Damage: A globally muted player cannot coordinate with their team (calling missing, Roshan timings, smoke ganks). This essentially punishes the 4 other innocent players on the team who are now playing at a severe disadvantage. 3. Impossible to Recover: Once a player's communication score drops, it is incredibly difficult to raise it back up because they cannot communicate to be commended, creating a vicious cycle. Suggested changes to rework the system: - Replace the forced absolute mute with a "soft mute". By default, the player is muted, but teammates should have a clear button to manually UNMUTE them if they want to coordinate. - Do not restrict essential gameplay pings and basic chat wheel commands for muted players. - Rework the automated penalty system so that report volume alone doesn't trigger immediate, severe communication bans without actual text/voice chat analysis. Please reconsider how this system operates, as it currently causes more frustration than it prevents. 4. Encouraging Griefing: The sudden in-game mute often demoralizes the team and triggers griefing behavior. For instance, in a recent match, immediately after a player received a system mute mid-game, two other teammates simply gave up and stopped playing entirely. The match instantly devolved into a chaotic, unplayable state, completely ruining the competitive integrity of the game. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 8949763997 ### Screenshots _No Dota 2 developers and community, I would like to ask for clarification regarding the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system. My current scores are: Behavior Score: 12,000 / 12,000 (maximum) Communication Score: 5,800 / 12,000 I regularly play Dota 2 and I do not intentionally grief, feed, destroy my items, abandon matches, throw games, or smurf. In ranked games, I play the roles assigned to me by the matchmaking system and try to play for the win. I also support Dota 2 financially and enjoy the game, which is why I would like to understand how this system works and how it could potentially be improved. I recently checked my Steam Personal Game Data → Dota 2 → Account → Incoming Match Player Report. My recent data shows Communication Reports even during periods where I had no abandons or excessive reports. For example: August 11: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 3 Communication Reports from 2 reporting parties August 8: - 15 matches - 14 positive matches - 1 reported match - 0 abandons - 4 Communication Reports from 3 reporting parties August 6: - 15 matches - 11 positive matches - 4 reported matches - 0 abandons - 7 total reports - 4 Communication Reports from 4 reporting parties August 2: - 15 matches - 15 positive matches - 0 reported matches - 0 abandons - 0 Communication Reports My main question is: How can a player have a maximum Behavior Score of 12,000/12,000 while having a Communication Score of only 5,800/12,000? I understand that these are separate systems and that Communication Reports can affect Communication Score. However, I am concerned about the possibility of unjustified or retaliatory reports. There is another situation that I believe is worth considering. In a five-player team, it is possible that three players are in the same party and know each other. If one of these players has a disagreement with me, the other two party members may potentially report me simply to support their friend, even if they did not personally witness any actual communication violation. In this situation, what could start as a disagreement between two players could potentially result in multiple reports against the same player simply because several players are grouped together. For example, instead of receiving one report from the player involved in the disagreement, I could potentially receive reports from all three members of the party because they want to support their friend. This raises an important question: Does the Communication Score system take party relationships or coordinated/retaliatory reporting into account? If multiple members of the same party report the same player, are these reports treated completely independently, or does the system recognize that they may be related to the same incident? I believe this is important because otherwise a single conflict between two players could potentially have a disproportionately large effect on another player's Communication Score. Players can report each other because of disagreements, frustration after losing a game, disagreements about gameplay decisions, or personal conflicts. Therefore, I would like to understand how the system prevents abuse of Communication Reports. I contacted Steam Support about this issue. They told me that the scores are automated and that Steam Support cannot manually adjust them. They also stated that they do not provide additional information about how the behavior scoring system is calculated. They recommended that I bring this issue to the Dota 2 community and development forums. So this is what I am doing. I am NOT asking for my Communication Score to be manually increased. I would simply like to understand whether the current system can incorrectly penalize a player because of unjustified, retaliatory, or potentially coordinated Communication Reports, and whether there are mechanisms that prevent players from abusing the reporting system. I would also like to raise another question regarding the recovery of Communication Score. Why does the Communication Score not have some form of regular recalibration or review period, for example once a year? Would it be possible to introduce an annual recalibration, review, or another mechanism that would give players who have demonstrated consistently good behavior over a long period of time a clearer way to recover their Communication Score? In my subjective opinion, there appears to be a significant imbalance between losing Communication Score and recovering it. It feels like a player can receive Communication Reports relatively easily and potentially lose Communication Score very quickly, while recovering that lost score through consistently good behavior appears to be much slower. Even if a player makes a serious effort to communicate politely and avoid violations over a long period of time, recovering from a low Communication Score can feel extremely difficult. In other words, the negative effect of reports can appear very quickly, while the positive effect of consistently good behavior takes much longer to become visible. I believe that a regular recalibration or another transparent recovery mechanism could make the system feel more fair. It would also give players a clearer motivation to improve their behavior because they would know that consistently good behavior over time can meaningfully restore their Communication Score. If there is no way for players to verify whether reports against them were legitimate, how can they know what behavior they need to change? I would appreciate any clarification from the Dota 2 developers or experienced players who understand how the current system works. I am not asking for special treatment for my account. I am asking whether the current system could be improved to make Communication Score more resistant to report abuse and to provide players with a reasonable path to recover from a low score through consistently good behavior. I have attached screenshots of my Personal Game Data as evidence. I hope that one day my partner, my children, and my warm friends can still be playing together when we're 40 or 50 years old. But it really hurts me. When I play with everyone else, because of my low behavior score, I get matched with these toxic teammates and have to endure 90-minute queue times. It forces me to leave the party again and again. Then I solo queue. And then in solo queue, I run into those racists and toxic players, wasting the few hundred behavior points I painstakingly accumulated. This vicious cycle is the biggest flaw of this great game. Over the past 2-3 years, I've tried everything I could. To escape this disgusting low behavior score player pool. I've tried. Believe me. Dota 2 Team. I would like to share feedback regarding the new Ranked matchmaking system after the latest update. I understand the goal of encouraging players to queue for all roles in order to reduce queue times and improve matchmaking. However, I believe the current implementation has the opposite effect on match quality. Previously, players had a choice. Those who preferred Ranked Roles could use them, while others could play Ranked Classic without role restrictions. Now, Ranked Roles are effectively the only option, and selecting preferred roles requires spending Role Queue Tokens that can only be earned by queuing for all roles. This creates several problems. First, many players are now forced to play roles they are neither comfortable with nor experienced on. For example, I mainly play ranged heroes as Carry, Mid, or Support. I do not enjoy playing Offlane or tank heroes, and I have significantly less experience on that role. When the system assigns me Offlane simply because I need to earn Role Queue Tokens, the quality of my performance is naturally much lower. This is not about refusing to cooperate or wanting to play only one role. It is about recognizing that players have different strengths. A player with thousands of games on Carry will not suddenly become a good Offlaner because the matchmaking system assigned that role. As a result, everyone loses: * the player is frustrated because they cannot play the role they enjoy; * teammates receive a weaker performance than they expected; * overall match quality decreases. Some players may even feel pressured to ignore their assigned role and switch lanes, creating arguments before the game has properly started and increasing the number of role abuse reports. This is an unhealthy incentive created by the system itself. The previous system allowed players to decide whether they wanted to earn tokens by playing every role. The new system removes that freedom and makes it effectively mandatory for anyone who wants to continue selecting preferred roles consistently. I believe there are better alternatives, such as: * bringing back Ranked Classic as an option; * allowing players to earn Role Queue Tokens by selecting one or more high-demand roles instead of all five; * providing additional ways to earn tokens without forcing players into roles they do not know how to play. I truly appreciate the work that goes into improving Dota 2, and I understand that reducing queue times is important. However, I believe that match quality should remain the highest priority. A shorter queue is not necessarily an improvement if it results in players being forced into roles where they cannot perform at their best. Thank you for taking the time to read this Description Dear Valve, I would like to share my experience with the behavior score system because I genuinely feel something is not working correctly in my case. Over the last several days, my behavior score has continued to decrease even though I play alone, focus on winning, and do my best to help my team. I don't understand why this is happening. I currently cannot even use chat, so I have no way to be toxic through text or voice communication. Despite that, my behavior score dropped from around 5,000 to about 4,000, and I received a 24-hour matchmaking ban. After this ban expires, I will most likely be placed into Low Priority, even though I don't believe I've done anything to deserve it. The most frustrating part is that I'm not a smurf or someone trying to ruin matches. I'm actually a relatively new player who wants to improve at Dota 2. I spend time learning heroes, watching guides, and trying to become a better teammate and player. I queue for ranked matches completely solo. Very often I get teammates who intentionally grief, give up early, or are simply much less experienced. Even in those situations, I keep playing until the end and sometimes manage to carry the game and win anyway. I don't abandon matches, I don't intentionally feed, and I always try my best regardless of how difficult the game becomes. Because of this, it's very confusing to see my behavior score constantly going down. It feels like I am being punished for something I didn't do. If players are reporting me simply because they are angry after a match or because I played differently than they expected, I hope those reports are being reviewed fairly. I understand that the behavior system is important for keeping the community healthy, and I support that goal. However, I also hope there is a way to identify cases where legitimate players are incorrectly losing behavior score. I would sincerely appreciate it if someone could review my account and the reports against it. If there has been a mistake, I kindly ask if my behavior score could be restored. Description I've been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I appreciate the effort Valve has put into improving the game. However, I believe there is an important issue with the current Overwatch and behavior systems that deserves attention. My main concern is that Overwatch reviewers may not always have enough context to accurately judge a player's actions. A single moment in a match can look like griefing without showing everything that happened beforehand. Sometimes a player is reacting to teammates who have been AFK farming, refusing to join fights, abandoning their role, or otherwise making the game extremely difficult to play. Without seeing the full progression of the match, it's easy to misinterpret those situations. I also think reports after a loss can sometimes be driven by frustration rather than actual griefing. If several players report someone simply because they lost, that player may repeatedly end up in the review system even if they were trying to win. I'm not saying the behavior system should be removed. I believe it is necessary. However, I think it could be improved by giving reviewers more context before making a decision and by continuing to refine how reports are evaluated. Some ideas that might help are: Allow reviewers to watch more of the match before and after the reported incident. Provide better timeline context for important events. Continue improving the detection of false or frustration-based reports. Ensure that players who consistently grief games are identified accurately while players who are genuinely trying to win are not punished unfairly. I enjoy Dota 2 and want the system to be as fair and accurate as possible. I hope this feedback is helpful and can contribute to future improvements. I can provide game id`s if necesary. Description ### Summary The current report and communication score system in Dota 2 feels too passive. Bad actors can severely insult opponents in All-Chat, ruin everyone's emotional state, and they only receive a minor score deduction matches later. We need a firmer, faster, and more transparent approach to protect the player base from toxicity. ### Why we need this (Balancing Environment and Player Retention) We understand that Valve needs to maintain its player base. Permanently banning or suspending accounts for chat toxicity can be counterproductive, as it drives players away entirely and ruins matchmaking times. Instead of banning the account, we should strictly "strip away their ability to ruin the game environment" while still letting them play the game. Keeping them in the game but forcing them into silence is the perfect balance for player retention and community health. ### Proposed Solutions 1. **Immediate All-Chat Time-out (Real-time Mitigation):** If the system detects severe toxic keywords or verified report spikes in All-Chat, that player should be instantly and automatically muted from All-Chat for the rest of the match or the next 24 hours. Stop the toxicity in its tracks before it spreads to other players. 2. **100% Automated System Reading (No Human Check Needed):** The system should automatically scan all chat logs using a pre-defined blocklist of toxic words, slurs, and toxic gaming jargon (e.g., "ez", "noob", "trash", "dog", etc.). There is no need for manual human checkers. If the text matches the filter, the penalty is executed immediately by the server. 3. **The "First-Striker" Principle (Protecting Those Who Reply):** Often, a toxic player starts the insults, and their teammates or opponents only reply out of frustration. The system should only punish the **first person** who initiates the toxic behavior in that specific chat timeline. Anyone who replies or defends themselves afterwards should NOT be penalized. Punishing the "first striker" stops the root cause of the toxicity without unfairly striking back at victims who are just reacting to provocation. 4. **Heavier Penalties for Severe Insults (-2000 Score):** Ruinous behavior shouldn't cost just 100 points. Severe toxic words should trigger a massive, immediate deduction (e.g., -2000 communication score). Since players lose All-Chat privileges when dropping below 10,000 points, one single toxic outburst should instantly silence them for dozens of matches until they earn it back. 5. **Transparency (Show the Evidence Log):** When players lose score, the client should show them a notification displaying exactly which log/words triggered the penalty. They need to know precisely *what* they typed that led to the punishment. Winning a game shouldn't be an excuse to demean opponents. Respecting the enemy team is basic sportsmanship, and Valve can enforce it strictly through precise, heavy chat restrictions without having to ban players from playing. ### Example Match ID (and Description ​The current Behavior Score system is detrimental to the Dota 2 experience. It fails to distinguish between unavoidable technical issues (power/internet outages, hardware failures) and intentional disruptive behavior. As a result, players are trapped in a "point of no return," where recovery is nearly impossible. ​The game is fundamentally a team-based experience, yet this system forces players into a state of "silent survival." Players are now terrified to use voice or text chat to coordinate, as any interaction can trigger retaliatory reports from teammates. This silence destroys the core of Dota 2, as communication is essential for team play. ​Furthermore, this system drives players to abandon their main accounts and create new ones, which devalues the competitive integrity of the game. ​Proposed Reforms: ​Remove the Hidden Behavior Score: Replace the current hidden point system with a transparent and predictable disciplinary model. ​Clear Penalties for Abandoning: Instead of a complex score reduction, implement direct consequences for technical issues. For example: 3 abandons = 5 games of Low Priority. ​Targeted Communication Bans: If a player receives reports from all 9 other players in a single match, they should receive a 48-hour communication ban. If the behavior persists, the punishment should escalate to Low Priority matches without access to chat for the purpose of "correction." ​Low Priority Revamp: Replace the mandatory "Single Draft" (SD) mode in Low Priority with "All Random" (AR). This makes the punishment less monotonous and keeps the game engaging, even for those serving time. ​Address Report Abuse and the Overwatch System: The current report system is heavily abused as a weapon against teammates. Furthermore, the "Overwatch" system is ineffective because reviewers often lack context or are biased, leading to unfair judgments. We need a system that filters out malicious, weaponized reports rather than penalizing any form of communication. ​The goal should be to encourage positive communication and team play, not to force players into "mute mode" or drive them away from the game entirely. I urge the development team to reconsider the current model in favor of a more transparent and fair disciplinary framework. I'd like to suggest a possible improvement to the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system. I wanted to share some feedback about the current Behavior Score and Communication Score system in Dota 2. The system has been in the game for almost three years now, and I think it has one major problem: once a player drops to a very low Behavior Score, it's extremely difficult to recover. You can play many games without abandoning or griefing and still gain only a small amount of Behavior Score. At the same time, it's very easy to lose hundreds of points from reports. Sometimes it feels like simply using chat is enough to get reported, even if you're just trying to communicate with your team. Because of this, many players can't use voice and text chat altogether. Others create new accounts just so they can play normally again, communicate with teammates, and queue for Ranked. I don't think that's the goal of the system. I think it would be worth considering some kind of amnesty or reset after all this time. Here are a few possible ideas: * Restore every account that isn't permanently banned to 12,000 Behavior Score and Communication Score. * If a full reset is too much, raise everyone below a certain threshold (for example, 8,000) to a healthier level. * Make Behavior Score recover much faster for players below 8,000, so they have a realistic chance to climb back. * Reduce Behavior Score losses from reports unless those reports are confirmed by the system. * Consider a one-time recovery event for long-term active players who haven't abandoned games or received confirmed griefing penalties for a long period. The system has already been in place for nearly three years. By now, players who wanted to improve their behavior have had plenty of time to do so. A one-time reset would give those players a fair chance to start over, while players who continue to be toxic would naturally lose their score again. The reason I'm suggesting this is simple. Right now, players with low Behavior Score often feel stuck. They can spend weeks trying to improve it and make almost no progress, while losing hundreds of points again after just a few matches. It becomes frustrating enough that many people simply stop playing on their main account. I also believe this would reduce the number of new accounts being created. Right now, many players feel that creating a new account is much easier than trying to recover their main account, and that's probably not the outcome the system was designed to encourage. I believe giving players another chance after almost three years would improve communication, reduce the number of new accounts being created, and make the system feel much fairer. Players who continue to be toxic would naturally lose their Behavior Score again, so the purpose of the system would remain the same. Description Description: Hello Valve Team, I am writing to report a critical issue with the current Behavior and Overwatch system at high-skill brackets (5000+ MMR). The system is heavily flawed and actively allows toxic account buyers, boosted profiles, and low-ranked reviewers to ruin the experience for legitimate high-tier players. I have over 6,000 hours of playtime and my Behavior Score has consistently stayed around 11,200+. Drops were rare and only occurred due to real-world power outages. However, within just two weeks, my score plummeted to 6,900, and I received 3 Low-Priority penalties back-to-back without breaking any rules. Here is the core problem with the current mechanics at 5000+ MMR: 1. Account Buyers & Rank-Boosted Toxicity: 5000+ MMR should represent high-tier gameplay. Instead, it is flooded with account buyers and boosted players who lack basic game sense, refuse to communicate, or make terrible decisions. When a legitimate player tries to coordinate the team using voice chat, these players submit malicious reports purely out of spite or to shift the blame for their own poor performance. 2. Incompetent Overwatch Reviewers: The system allows lower-ranked players (whose understanding of high-level Dota is completely lacking) to review Overwatch cases for high-MMR matches. They evaluate high-tier item builds or non-meta draft choices based on their own low-rank templates, resulting in unjustified "Guilty" verdicts for griefing. 3. Automated LP Triggers: Just yesterday, after receiving a notification that my score dropped due to reports, I logged into the game today without playing a single match only to find myself with a 3-game Single Draft penalty. The system acts automatically based on raw report volume rather than factual gameplay abuse. Please review the matchmaking reporting system algorithms. Legitimate high-MMR players should not have their accounts restricted because of malicious reports from account buyers or the incorrect verdicts of low-skilled Overwatch reviewers. He effectively fed gold to the enemy team the entire game. His final score of 9/9/3 is misleading, as he only secured those kills at the very end of the match while the rest of the team was trying to push the enemy Ancient without him. Throughout the match, I tried to communicate with him via voice chat without any aggression, calmly asking him to play with the team. Instead of listening, this player and other low-skill allies submitted malicious reports against me simply because I pointed out his lack of impact. Additional Information The issue started immediately after the 27 June 2026 update. Other Steam games launch and run normally. Windows Event Viewer records no application crash. Description # **The Current Player Behavior System Creates Silent Matches and Makes Recovery Nearly Impossible** I have been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I believe the current Player Behavior Summary system has serious flaws that are damaging the quality of matches and the social experience of the game. For nearly a year, my Behavior Score has remained around 3000. During this time, I have had very limited communication privileges, rarely communicate with other players, do not abandon matches, and do not intentionally grief games. Despite this, my score barely changes and meaningful recovery appears almost impossible. The main issue is that the system does not seem to adequately distinguish between intentional griefing and simply having a bad game. When a team loses, frustrated players often report their teammates. A player can make mistakes, have a poor performance, or simply be unlucky without intentionally ruining the match. However, those reports still contribute to a punishment system that can trap players at low Behavior Scores for extremely long periods of time. Another consequence is that many matches have become completely silent. Players are afraid to communicate because they fear reports and further penalties. Others have already lost access to communication features. As a result, matches often contain: * No leadership * No strategic discussion * No coordination * No planning * No meaningful social interaction Dota 2 is fundamentally a team game. Communication is one of its most important elements. A system designed to improve player behavior should not create an environment where players are afraid to speak. My questions to the Dota team are: 1. How does the system distinguish between intentional griefing and simply performing poorly? 2. How is a player expected to recover from a very low Behavior Score if reports continue to outweigh positive behavior? 3. Is the current system achieving its intended goal, or is it simply creating silent matches where players avoid communication altogether? I understand the need to punish toxic behavior, intentional griefing, and abusive communication. However, the current system appears excessively punitive and offers very little transparency regarding how players can realistically recover.
